title: Qunova Computing Achieves Chemical Accuracy at 80 Qubits on Iron-Sulfur Cluster Using IBM Quantum System Two and Fugaku - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Qunova Computing ran its HI-VQE hybrid algorithm across IBM Quantum System Two and RIKEN's Fugaku to reach chemical accuracy (within 1.6 mHa of DMRG) on an 80-qubit [4Fe-4S] iron-sulfur cluster simulation, while cutting classical supercomputer cost ~300x versus prior SQD runs. The result positions quantum-centric supercomputing as moving from demos toward quantitative chemistry on strongly correlated systems.

insights.claim: Qunova Computing demonstrated chemical accuracy in an 80-qubit electronic-structure simulation of the [4Fe-4S] iron-sulfur cubane cluster using a hybrid workflow across an IBM Quantum System Two processor and RIKEN's Fugaku supercomputer.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A South Korean algorithm startup is claiming a quantitative chemistry milestone on IBM hardware, strengthening the hybrid quantum-HPC narrative.
insights.locator: South Korean quantum algorithm developer Qunova

insights.claim: Qunova's HI-VQE run produced an extrapolated ground-state energy of -327.2482 ± 0.0007 Hartree, within chemical accuracy (1.6 mHa, about 1 kcal/mol) of the classical DMRG reference of -327.2471 Ha.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Matching a gold-standard classical benchmark is the threshold for quantum chemistry results to be taken seriously by industrial users.

insights.claim: Reaching quantitative chemical accuracy at 80 qubits had been an open milestone, since earlier quantum-centric supercomputing experiments only demonstrated subspace sampling on smaller active spaces.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals the field crossing from qualitative demos toward scale where results could matter commercially.
insights.quote: reaching quantitative chemical accuracy at 80 qubits has remained an open milestone
insights.locator: Transition-metal complexes such as iron-sulfur clusters

insights.claim: Qunova's 80-qubit run used 2,518 Fugaku node-hours, which the article describes as an approximately 300x reduction in classical compute cost versus prior sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Classical HPC cost is a hidden bottleneck in hybrid quantum workflows; a 300x cut materially improves the economics.

insights.claim: HI-VQE couples quantum state sampling with classical subspace diagonalization without relying on linearity or spatial locality assumptions, which Qunova says makes it applicable across catalysts, battery electrodes and pharmaceutical targets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Generality across chemistry domains broadens the addressable market for the algorithm.
insights.quote: without relying on linearity or spatial locality assumptions

insights.claim: Iron-sulfur clusters such as [4Fe-4S] are the catalytic core of nitrogenase and hydrogenase enzymes and are considered intractable for exact classical solvers because their strongly correlated electrons challenge density functional theory.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: These are commercially relevant targets (nitrogen fixation, clean hydrogen) where classical methods fall short, a plausible early-advantage niche.
insights.locator: Transition-metal complexes such as iron-sulfur clusters

insights.claim: Qunova plans to add orbital rotation and optimization routines to future HI-VQE releases so it can process between 500 million and 3 billion unique electronic configurations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Roadmap signals scaling ambition; watch whether subsequent releases deliver at that configuration count.
insights.quote: process between 500 million and 3 billion unique electronic configurations

insights.claim: The Qunova work was supported by Japan's NEDO Post-5G quantum-HPC hybrid platform initiative, and HI-VQE is already distributed via IBM's Qiskit Functions Catalog and the AWS Marketplace for Amazon Braket.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Government funding plus multi-cloud distribution indicates a commercialization path beyond a single hardware vendor.
